title: Investigate TTFT anomaly: worker-affinity mismatch causing token throughput collapse
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported sudden TTFT regressions and sharp drops in tokens/sec across hosted and dedicated clusters starting 2026-03-09. Symptoms: elevated first-token and tail latencies for short-chat and rerank workloads; throughput drops by up to 60% on affected hosts. Issue appears multi-tenant and model-agnostic but concentrated on nodes running mixed-precision and mixed-model pools. Urgent investigation required to identify root cause, mitigate customer impact, and ship a hotfix with minimal risk to capacity.
steps_taken: 03-09 03:20: Collected traces from affected clusters (tracing IDs: trace-redwood-20260309-01)
03-09 04:00: Rolled partial routing rule to avoid one problematic pool for select customers (manual mitigation)
03-10 09:15: Correlated TTFT spikes with `worker_affinity` churn events and frequent micro-scaling actions in autoscaler logs
03-11 13:40: Captured pprof CPU profiles and per-worker KV-cache hit/miss rates; retrieved kernel selector logs
03-12 21:05: Replayed representative production traffic in staging with identical model mixes and observed throughput collapse reproducibly
findings: Affinity churn: worker-affinity heuristics are oscillating under mixed-model routing, causing frequent cold starts of KV caches and repeated model kernel re-preparation
Batching disruption: continuous small-scale rebalances reduced effective batching windows, increasing per-token overhead and reducing tokens/sec
KV cache fragmentation: cache partitions for large-context models are being evicted unexpectedly when workers migrate, increasing recompute on hot prefixes
Autoscaler interplay: aggressive min/max scaling configuration for some Dedicated pools causes repeated short-duration scale ups/downs that amplify affinity churn
Scope: affects Hosted and Dedicated primarily; Private clusters observed only when operators enabled multi-model multiplexing policy
proposed_fix: Stabilize worker-affinity and reduce churn via a two-part approach: (1) introduce a short sticky period (configurable) where worker-affinity decisions are stabilized for 15s to 60s to allow KV cache warmup and batching to amortize; (2) add a hysteresis rule to autoscaler to avoid scaling for fluctuations under 20% for <30s. Implement conservative default values and expose tuning in Dedicated/Private configs.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement sticky-affinity + autoscaler hysteresis in runtime (branch: feat/affinity-stabilizer)
2) Run canary on staging and a low-traffic Hosted region for 24h with synthetic traffic generator mimicking customer mixes
3) Gradual ramp: enable on 5% of production hosts -> 25% -> 100% over 48 hours while monitoring TTFT and tokens/sec metrics
4) For Dedicated customers with strict SLAs, offer opt-in staged upgrade and provide rollback flag
5) Post-rollout: run a 7-day quality monitor and alert on any >10% tokens/sec regression vs baseline
rollback_criteria: Increase in 95th percentile TTFT by >20% compared to pre-rollout baseline
Reduction in global tokens/sec by >15% sustained for 30 minutes
Unanticipated increase in error rates (5xx) or model inference failures
Any customer-reported critical impact escalations during rollout window
